subject.title: feat: cross-gateway sessions_send and sessions_spawn via gateway.peers

question: Should OpenClaw core accept `gateway.peers` session-tool routing now, and what identity, credential, scope, replay, and transcript-ownership contract must gate it?
rationale: The PR changes a Gateway trust boundary and adds config-backed secret use from model-facing tools; automation cannot safely decide the product/security contract.

options.title: Define the federation contract first
options.body: Keep the PR open or paused while maintainers define the peer trust, URL policy, idempotency, and session-state contract, then require the branch to implement that contract.

options.title: Narrow and land `gateway.peers`
options.body: Accept the proposed shape after fixing the blocking defects, resolving conflicts, requiring explicit peer credentials or an approved auth-none mode, and adding real multi-gateway proof.

options.title: Defer to the FRD
options.body: Close or pause this PR in favor of the broader federation tracker if maintainers want bridge protocol and cross-gateway identity primitives before session-tool routing.

recommendation.title: Define the federation contract first
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open or paused while maintainers define the peer trust, URL policy, idempotency, and session-state contract, then require the branch to implement that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest observed history across the session-tool semantics and gateway URL/security boundary this PR changes.
